comparator.name: Human Movement Sciences (Bewegingswetenschappen)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted OER 2026–27, articles 10–12 and current 2026–27 study guide; checked 2026-09-25
comparator.sourceNotes: Article 10.2 states that the bachelor has no formal route or specialisation. Article 11.3 lists ten compulsory 6-EC first-year modules and ten compulsory 6-EC second-year modules, then compulsory 6-EC advanced movement-system anatomy and the 24-EC bachelor research project. Article 12 reserves at least 30 EC for a genuinely open approved minor or elective package; specific sport, health or mental-health minors are optional examples, not compulsory tracks. The zero-credit language test is excluded from 180 EC. VU requires biomechanics, mechanical analysis, exercise and muscle physiology, practical movement measurements and clinical movement analysis that UCR does not offer as a matched sequence.

alternatives.concept: Combines functional anatomy and physiology with perception and action, movement-related health, mathematical signal methods and data analysis. It offers an interdisciplinary route into movement questions while retaining the absence of dedicated biomechanics, exercise physiology labs and clinical gait analysis.

alternatives.concept: Explores movement and recovery through brain and behaviour, anatomy, physiology, medical and clinical psychology, development and the philosophy of mind and emotion. It retains data and experimental research but gives more space to psychological dimensions than to mechanics and signal modelling.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Four courses in the measurement-focused route (linear algebra, numerical methods, signal systems and probability theory) give way to abnormal psychology, psychodiagnostics, philosophy of mind and philosophy of emotion. This is a substantive 30-EC shift from physical quantification toward psychological health and recovery, while the shared anatomy, brain and research foundations remain visible.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The integrated anatomy, brain, measurement and health curriculum is the closest feasible response, though biomechanical and exercise-specific laboratory work remains unmatched. A second evidence-backed route shifts 30 EC from physical quantification to psychological health and behaviour; the course choices are substantively different and feasible. A proposed athletic training/performance physiology route would require a coherent set of specialised exercise physiology, training load, sport injury and biomechanics courses that the UCR workbook does not provide, so no third 24-course alternative is claimed.

notes.text: VU requires specialised biomechanics, muscle and exercise physiology, clinical movement analysis and measurement laboratories, plus a 24-EC empirical bachelor research project. UCR offers interdisciplinary anatomy, general physiology, neuroscience, psychology and quantitative/data methods, without reproducing that specialist lab progression. The 30-EC VU minor remains open in the comparator.
